# Udayajātaka (Ja 458)

**ID:** Ja 458  
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Udayajātaka  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul10.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul10.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Ruling the prosperous city of Surundha, the couple maintain a life of absolute celibacy (*brahmacariya*) in a shared chamber for seven hundred years without succumbing to lust [Fausböll 1887; Silk 2009]. After dying first, the Bodhisatta is reborn as Sakka; he subsequently tests the queen's virtue, teaches her the Dhamma, and inspires her to renounce the world as an ascetic, where upon death she is reborn in the Tāvatiṃsa heaven [Fausböll 1887]. At the conclusion of the sermon, the backsliding monk attains stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1887].

 Beyond the Pali tradition, the narrative was adapted into Sanskrit kavya in the *Haribhaṭṭajātakamālā* (*Udayajātaka*) [Martin 2006], and early visual depictions of the story are preserved among the Hinayana wall paintings of Cave 9 at Ajanta [Spink 2006].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: SN 1.75 Bhītāsutta; SA2 314 栴檀; SA 1315 栴檀
- Mentioned in: Ne 37 Sāsanapaṭṭhāna

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1887] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka together with its Commentary, Vol. IV (1887) — Pali text and commentary of the Udayajātaka, narrative details, and conclusion.
- [Silk 2009] Jonathan A. Silk, Riven by Lust: Incest and Schism in Indian Buddhist Legend and Historiography (2009) — Analysis of the royal sibling marriage and narrative parallels.
- [Martin 2006] Dan Martin, Tibeto-Sanskrit Philology Bibliography (2006) — Reference to Michael Hahn's edition of the Haribhaṭṭajātakamālā's Udayajātaka.
- [Spink 2006] Walter M. Spink, Ajanta: History and Development, Vol. II (2006) — Identification of Udaya Jātaka paintings in Cave 9 at Ajanta.
